Billing v2 - design notes

Goal
Replace the monthly invoice batch with per-account billing runs that can be replayed. Every run reads the ledger
snapshot at 00:00 UTC and writes invoices, credit notes and the reconciliation report to the Billing v2 folder.

Decisions so far
1. Invoices are immutable once issued; corrections are credit notes.
2. Tax rates come from the finance table, never from the account record.
3. Runs are idempotent: re-running a day produces byte-identical documents.
4. The vendor comparison (see the PDF in this folder) settled on the in-house renderer.

Open questions
- Who approves credit notes above 2,000? Proposal: finance lead plus the account owner.
- Do we keep the legacy batch for six months or three?
- Which accounts need the invoice schedule sheet reviewed before go-live?

Next steps
Sam drafts the schema changes; Dana updates the invoice schedule; kickoff deck review on Thursday.
Reviewers: Sam Okafor, Priya Natarajan (external), finance@example.test (group).

Appendix: the reconciliation report lists every account with its opening balance, charges, payments and closing
balance, grouped by currency. Discrepancies above 0.01 are flagged for manual review; the report is a Google Sheet
generated per run and linked from the run summary. Retention: seven years, in line with the finance policy.

Slide 1 - Billing v2 kickoff
Replayable per-account billing runs. Target: first production run on 1 October 2026.

Slide 2 - Why now
The monthly batch fails silently on partial ledgers; finance reconciles by hand for two days each month.

Slide 3 - Scope
Invoices, credit notes, reconciliation report, invoice schedule. Out of scope: dunning, collections.

Slide 4 - Team
Dana Reyes (lead), Sam Okafor (schema and runs), Priya Natarajan (external review), finance group (approvals).

Slide 5 - Timeline
Sep 14 kickoff - Sep 25 schema freeze - Oct 1 first run - Oct 15 retro.

Slide 6 - Risks
Tax table drift; renderer fonts; legacy batch overlap during the first month.



# Platform roadmap (H2 2026)

## Themes

1. **Reliability first** - error budgets per service, paged only on customer-visible symptoms.
2. **Observability** - one trace id from the edge to the ledger; structured logs everywhere; dashboards per team.
3. **Billing v2** - replayable runs (see the Billing v2 folder under Projects).
4. **Self-serve onboarding** - the checklist becomes an in-product flow.

## Q3

- Migrate the remaining batch jobs to the scheduler.
- Ship the observability pipeline: OpenTelemetry collectors in every cluster, sampling at 10 percent.
- Billing v2 schema freeze.

## Q4

- Billing v2 first production run (1 October) and retro.
- Deprecate the legacy invoice batch after one clean month.
- Cost review: storage tiers for archives older than a year.

## Not doing

- Multi-region writes (revisit in 2027).
- A second data warehouse.

## Owners

Dana Reyes (platform), Sam Okafor (billing), the design system group (self-serve onboarding).

## Notes

Every item links to a tracking issue; this document is the narrative, not the source of truth. Updated on the
first Monday of each month; ping Dana for edits.

2025 retro

What went well: the scheduler migration, the offsite, fewer pages in December.
What did not: the invoice batch, the archive cleanup, too many dashboards nobody reads.
Actions: replayable billing runs; one dashboard per team; archive policy.

Team handbook

Welcome. This handbook is shared with anyone who has the link so contractors and candidates can read it.

How we work
- Written first: decisions live in documents, meetings confirm them.
- Working hours are flexible; core overlap is 10:00-15:00 in the team's main zone.
- Every change to production goes through review; no exceptions for emergencies (use the incident channel).

Communication
- Async by default. Tag the owner, not the whole channel.
- Weekly notes are published every Monday morning and archived in the Meeting notes documents.
- Decisions are recorded with a date, the options considered and who decided.

Tools
- Drive for documents and sheets; the Projects folder holds anything with a deadline.
- The design system lives in Sam's folder and is shared with the platform team as editors.
- The onboarding checklist is visible to everyone in the domain.

Leave and travel
- Book leave two weeks ahead where possible; offsites are announced a quarter ahead.
- Expense reports are a spreadsheet per month, reviewed by the team lead.

Security
- Hardware keys for every account. Never share links to files marked confidential.
- Report lost devices within the hour.

Reading list
- The platform roadmap (Projects folder).
- The 2025 retro (archived).
- The billing v2 design notes once you join that project.

Questions go to Dana Reyes. This document is updated quarterly; the last review was in August 2026.

Onboarding checklist

Day 1
- Laptop, hardware key, accounts (mail, Drive, calendar, issue tracker).
- Read the team handbook.
- Meet your buddy.

Week 1
- Ship one small change with review.
- Join the weekly notes; add a line about what you learned.
- Set up the local environment for the platform repo.

Month 1
- Own one small project end to end.
- Present a ten-minute lightning talk.
- Give feedback on this checklist.

Owner: Dana Reyes. Visible to everyone at example.test.





Meeting notes 2026-09-10

Attendees: Dana, Sam, Ravi (intern).

Topics
1. Billing v2 schema: Sam walked through the account and invoice tables; Dana asked for the credit note flow.
2. Offsite photos: Sam shared the folder; Dana to pick three for the newsletter.
3. Intern project: Ravi will tidy the archive folder and propose a retention policy.

Decisions
- Schema freeze stays on 25 September.
- Credit notes reference the original invoice id; no partial invoices.

Actions
- Sam: publish the schema doc by Friday.
- Dana: review the invoice schedule sheet.
- Ravi: draft the retention policy in a new document.

Next meeting: 12 September.

Meeting notes 2026-09-12

Attendees: Dana, Sam.

Topics
1. Schema doc published; Dana reviewed the credit note section.
2. Kickoff deck: slide 6 risks need the legacy overlap plan.
3. Vendor comparison: in-house renderer confirmed.

Decisions
- Kickoff on Monday 14 September at 10:00.
- Sam becomes editor on the Billing v2 folder (already shared).

Actions
- Dana: finish the deck.
- Sam: prepare the demo data set.

Next meeting: 17 September.



Q3 planning notes

Owner: Sam Okafor. Shared with Dana as a viewer.

Objectives
1. Billing v2 schema frozen and reviewed.
2. Design system tokens published as JSON and consumed by two apps.
3. Component inventory complete with owners and status.

Key results
- Schema review sign-off from platform and finance by 25 September.
- Tokens file (Tokens.json) published from the Design system folder; version 1.2.
- Inventory sheet lists every component with a usage count and an owner.

Risks
- Finance review capacity in September.
- Token naming changes ripple into two apps.

Weekly checkpoints on Fridays; notes appended below.

Week 36: schema draft circulated. Week 37: kickoff scheduled; inventory at 70 percent.
